learn.rule: Combine short sentences into one smooth sentence. Keep every fact and do not repeat words.
learn.ruleEs: Combina oraciones cortas en una oración fluida. Conserva todos los datos y no repitas palabras.
learn.model: Owls hunt at night and have great eyesight.
learn.notice: Two short sentences became one. The word Owls is only said once.

items.prompt: Which sentence joins the two facts about owls?
items.text: Owls hunt at night. Owls have great eyesight.

options.text: Owls hunt at night owls have great eyesight.
Owls hunt at night and have great eyesight.
Owls hunt at night.

items.why: This one keeps both facts and joins them with and. The first runs together, and the last drops a fact.
items.whyEs: Esta conserva los dos datos y los une con and. La primera está pegada, y la última pierde un dato.

items.prompt: Which sentence about the whale has no repeated words?
items.text: The whale is huge. The whale is gentle.

options.text: The whale is huge and the whale is gentle.
The whale is huge and gentle.
The whale huge gentle.

items.why: When both sentences share the same subject and verb, say them once and join the describing words.
items.whyEs: Cuando las dos oraciones tienen el mismo sujeto y verbo, dilos una vez y une las palabras que describen.

items.prompt: Join the penguin facts: Penguins cannot fly. They swim very well.
items.model: Penguins cannot fly, but they swim very well.
items.why: Not flying and swimming well are a contrast, so but joins them.
items.whyEs: No volar y nadar muy bien son un contraste, así que but los une.

items.prompt: Join the spider facts: Spiders have eight legs. Spiders spin silk.
items.model: Spiders have eight legs and spin silk.
items.why: Both facts are just added together, so and joins them. Spiders is not repeated.
items.whyEs: Los dos datos solo se suman, así que and los une. Spiders no se repite.

items.prompt: Check every sentence that keeps both shark facts. Facts: Sharks live in the ocean. Sharks have sharp teeth.

options.text: Sharks live in the ocean and have sharp teeth.
Sharks live in the ocean.
Sharks have sharp teeth and live in the ocean.
Sharks with sharp teeth.

items.why: Two sentences keep both facts, in either order. The others lose a fact or are not whole sentences.
items.whyEs: Dos oraciones conservan los dos datos, en cualquier orden. Las otras pierden un dato o no son oraciones completas.

items.prompt: Which sentence combines the melting ice facts with the right meaning?
items.text: The ice melted. The sun came out.

options.text: The ice melted so the sun came out.
The ice melted but the sun came out.
The ice melted because the sun came out.

items.why: The sun is the reason the ice melted, so because keeps the meaning true.
items.whyEs: El sol es la razón por la que se derritió el hielo, así que because mantiene el significado correcto.

write.prompt: Combine these three short sentences into one smooth sentence. Keep all the facts.
write.promptEs: Combina estas tres oraciones cortas en una oración fluida. Conserva todos los datos.
write.text: Bees make honey. Bees live in hives. Bees work together.

label: I kept the fact about honey
Conservé el dato de honey
I kept the fact about hives
Conservé el dato de hives
I kept the fact about working together
Conservé el dato de trabajar juntas

write.model: Bees live in hives, make honey, and work together.

familyTalk.en: Say two short sentences about a pet or an animal. Then join them into one sentence with and, but, or because.
familyTalk.es: Digan dos oraciones cortas sobre una mascota o un animal. Luego únanlas en una con and, but o because.

teacherTip.en: Have students read the short sentences aloud, then the combined one, and say which sounds smoother.
teacherTip.es: Pide que lean en voz alta las oraciones cortas y luego la combinada, y que digan cuál suena más fluida.

learn.rule: Combine short sentences into one smooth sentence. Keep every fact and do not repeat words.
learn.ruleEs: Combina oraciones cortas en una oración fluida. Conserva todos los datos y no repitas palabras.
learn.model: Ms. Lee drives a bus and greets every student.
learn.notice: The name Ms. Lee appears once, and both facts are still there.

items.prompt: Which sentence joins the two facts about Ms. Lee?
items.text: Ms. Lee drives a bus. Ms. Lee is very kind.

options.text: Ms. Lee drives a bus she is very kind.
Ms. Lee drives a bus.
Ms. Lee drives a bus and is very kind.

items.why: It keeps both facts and says Ms. Lee only once.
items.whyEs: Conserva los dos datos y dice Ms. Lee una sola vez.

items.prompt: Which sentence about the park has no repeated words?
items.text: The park is big. The park is green.

options.text: The park is big and the park is green.
The park is big and green.
The park big green is.

items.why: The park is big and green says each word once and keeps both facts.
items.whyEs: The park is big and green dice cada palabra una vez y conserva los dos datos.

items.prompt: Join the facts: Carlos has a big game. He practices every day.
items.model: Carlos has a big game, so he practices every day.
items.why: Practicing is the result of having a big game, so so is the right joiner.
items.whyEs: Practicar es el resultado de tener un juego importante, así que so es la palabra correcta.

items.prompt: Join the facts: The market is busy. The line moves fast.
items.model: The market is busy, but the line moves fast.
items.why: A busy market usually has a slow line, so a fast line is a contrast. But joins it.
items.whyEs: Un mercado lleno suele tener una fila lenta, así que una fila rápida es un contraste. But la une.

items.prompt: Check every sentence that keeps both library facts. Facts: The library is quiet. The library has comfy chairs.

options.text: The library is quiet and has comfy chairs.
The library has comfy chairs.
The quiet library has comfy chairs.
The library is quiet or has comfy chairs.

items.why: Both right answers keep quiet and comfy chairs. Or would change the meaning, and the other drops a fact.
items.whyEs: Las dos respuestas correctas conservan quiet y comfy chairs. Or cambiaría el significado, y la otra pierde un dato.

items.prompt: Which sentence is the best way to combine the three bus facts?
items.text: We ride a bus. The bus is yellow. The bus is old.

options.text: We ride a bus yellow old.
We ride an old yellow bus.
We ride a bus. Yellow and old.

items.why: Describing words can move in front of the noun. All three facts stay in one smooth sentence.
items.whyEs: Las palabras que describen pueden ir antes del sustantivo. Los tres datos quedan en una sola oración fluida.

write.prompt: Combine these three short sentences into one smooth sentence. Keep all the facts.
write.promptEs: Combina estas tres oraciones cortas en una oración fluida. Conserva todos los datos.
write.text: Our class has a garden. We grow tomatoes. We water the plants every day.

label: I kept the fact about the garden
Conservé el dato del jardín
I kept the fact about tomatoes
Conservé el dato de los tomates
I kept the fact about watering
Conservé el dato del riego

write.model: Our class has a garden where we grow tomatoes and water the plants every day.

familyTalk.en: Pick three short facts about your street. Join them into one sentence together.
familyTalk.es: Elijan tres datos cortos sobre su calle. Únanlos juntos en una sola oración.

teacherTip.en: Have partners work together to cut repeated words. Compare their smoothest versions.
teacherTip.es: Pide que las parejas trabajen juntas para quitar palabras repetidas. Comparen las versiones más fluidas.

learn.rule: Combine short sentences into one smooth sentence. Keep every fact and do not repeat words.
learn.ruleEs: Combina oraciones cortas en una oración fluida. Conserva todos los datos y no repitas palabras.
learn.model: Lena wrote a poem and read it aloud.
learn.notice: The word it stands in for the poem, so the poem is not said twice.

items.prompt: Which sentence joins the two story facts about the dragon?
items.text: The dragon was tired. The dragon flew home.

options.text: The dragon was tired and the dragon flew home.
The dragon was tired he flew home.
The dragon was tired, so he flew home.

items.why: It keeps both facts, shows the result with so, and uses he instead of repeating the dragon.
items.whyEs: Conserva los dos datos, muestra el resultado con so y usa he en vez de repetir the dragon.

items.prompt: Which sentence about Lena's poem combines the two sentences without repeating words?
items.text: Lena wrote a poem. Lena read the poem aloud.

options.text: Lena wrote a poem and read it aloud.
Lena wrote a poem and Lena read the poem aloud.
Lena wrote a poem read the poem aloud.

items.why: It says Lena once and uses it for the poem, so nothing is repeated.
items.whyEs: Dice Lena una vez y usa it para el poema, así que no se repite nada.

items.prompt: Join the facts: The map was old. It still showed the way.
items.model: The map was old, but it still showed the way.
items.why: An old map might not work, so showing the way is a contrast. But joins it.
items.whyEs: Un mapa viejo podría no servir, así que mostrar el camino es un contraste. But lo une.

items.prompt: Join the facts: The pirate found a chest. He opened it.
items.model: The pirate found a chest and opened it.
items.why: One action follows the other, so and joins them. The pirate is said once.
items.whyEs: Una acción sigue a la otra, así que and las une. The pirate se dice una vez.

items.prompt: Check every sentence that keeps all of Pablo's facts. Facts: Pablo has a drum. The drum is red. Pablo plays it in the parade.

options.text: Pablo plays his red drum in the parade.
Pablo has a drum.
Pablo has a red drum, and he plays it in the parade.
Pablo plays a drum in the parade.

items.why: The right ones keep the drum, the red color and the parade. The others leave out facts.
items.whyEs: Las correctas conservan el tambor, el color rojo y el desfile. Las otras omiten datos.

items.prompt: Which sentence is the best combination of the autumn facts?
items.text: The wind blew. The leaves fell. The leaves were orange.

options.text: The wind blew and the orange leaves fell.
The wind blew and the leaves fell.
The wind blew and the leaves fell and the leaves were orange.

items.why: It keeps the wind, the falling and the orange color in one clear sentence.
items.whyEs: Conserva el viento, la caída y el color naranja en una sola oración clara.

write.prompt: Combine these three short sentences into one smooth sentence. Keep all the facts.
write.promptEs: Combina estas tres oraciones cortas en una oración fluida. Conserva todos los datos.
write.text: The rabbit was fast. The rabbit was brave. The rabbit crossed the river.
write.model: The fast, brave rabbit crossed the river.

familyTalk.en: Tell a story in three tiny sentences. Then join them into one smooth sentence.
familyTalk.es: Cuenten un cuento en tres oraciones muy cortas. Luego únanlas en una oración fluida.

teacherTip.en: Ask students which word they dropped when they combined, and why it was safe to drop.
teacherTip.es: Pregunta qué palabra quitaron al combinar y por qué era seguro quitarla.
